dedupe_keys.name: finesse agent based financial event sequence simulator and finesse bench dataset

description: FINESSE (Financial Event Sequence Simulation Environment) is an agent-based simulation framework that generates synthetic, structured datasets of several interdependent event streams for financial services, such as card transactions, payments, account status changes and policy interventions, each with its own action space, schema and variable types, coupled through the agents' evolving latent states. With it comes FINESSE-Bench, a benchmark dataset supporting balance forecasting, transaction fraud detection, missed payment prediction and next event prediction, with baselines from time series, event sequence, temporal graph and point process methods. It was developed by Tyler Farnan, Benjamin Eng, Adam Abate, Xirui Hou, Rizal Fathony, Nam H. Nguyen and Senthil Kumar of Capital One and posted on arXiv on 9 September 2026. Coverage is synthetic and generic. Licence: not stated for the code (no LICENSE file in the GitHub repository); paper under the arXiv non-exclusive licence; the Hugging Face dataset requires sign-in. Caveats: the data are simulated, and realism depends on the behaviour models chosen; the release is new and not yet peer reviewed. For simulation it provides an agent-based generator of customer financial behaviour for testing how payment disruptions, policy changes or fraud spread through account-level events. It is related to the IBM AMLworld synthetic transactions record in this catalogue, another synthetic financial benchmark.
